Wind-flagged Araucaria stand, forty trunks leaning east at fifteen degrees, every branch stripped bare on the windward side and swept into dark blue-green fans pointing downwind, snow packed hard against the lee bark, copper lichen burning small and warm on the lowest exposed root.

Krummholz mat of ancient podocarp, centuries compressed flat across granite pavement, no trunk rising more than knee-height, the whole mass silvered and wind-tortured, snow drifted through its labyrinth in cobalt blue channels, one rust-orange scrub stem catching the only colour in the grey rock field.

Two-hundred-foot Araucaria cathedral, eight trunks black-wet in a cathedral row, boughs sagging under snow loads thicker than the boughs carrying them, the shadow between trunks a deep cobalt trench, low pale sun striking the topmost snow-laden tier white-bright against a slate sky.

The tree-line edge mid-slope, dense dark-needle forest stopping clean along a horizontal band, bare snowfield and fractured rock stretching above it, three solitary survivor conifers standing fifty yards past the line alone, small and dark against the open white, the sky above them empty and hard blue.

Frost-rimed giant podocarp, every needle on its sixty-foot spread furred in hoarfrost crystal, the whole crown glittering under thin winter sun, breath-fog cold condensing visibly at the base, one cluster of old cones showing a faint ochre glow deep inside the rime-whitened branch mass.

Avalanche scar bisecting the slope, a hundred-yard swath of snapped Araucaria trunks silvered and bare, the break-lines jagged at chest height, young conifer seedlings pushing six inches through the snow in the gap, their needles vivid dark blue-green against the white debris field.

Cloud-layer forest, the upper canopy of a podocarp stand piercing a cloud deck at roughly a thousand feet, the top third of each massive trunk and its snow-loaded crown floating in cold white silence above the cloud, the lower forest dissolved entirely, only the emergent tops visible, pale sun striking them from above.

Krummholz field at the true tree-line, ancient Araucaria individuals pressed flat into the rock, their trunks no thicker than a forearm yet four centuries old, ice crystals filling every joint in the mat, one dead stem showing copper-needled rust warm against the surrounding blue-white granite.

Snow-loaded mega-conifer grove, podocarp boughs so deep under load they touch the snowpack below, forming white-roofed vaults higher than the boulders they bridge, the interior dim and cold and blue, icicles six feet long hanging from the lowest boughs, the trunks near-black and dripping.

Wind-flagged stand of ancient conifers, trunks spaced wide across exposed ridgeline, every crown reduced to a wind-combed pennant streaming east, the westward bark pale and abraded, snowpack built in a long hard wedge on the eastern side of each trunk, amber low sun on the far ridge small and precise.

Frost-rimed conifer cathedral, two-hundred-year-old Araucaria with each of its horizontal tiers completely whitened by hoarfrost, the branch architecture rendered visible in white crystal, dark trunk contrasting deep and wet below, low-angle light splitting into prismatic cold sparkle across the top tier, everything breathing cold.

Moss and lichen rock garden under dense canopy, five house-sized boulders in a cluster, their faces furred in frozen dark moss and pale grey-green lichen, meltwater that crept across them overnight now glazed as clear ice sheets, the cobalt shadow under each boulder deeper than the surrounding forest floor.

The tree-line itself on a north-facing slope, the last continuous forest ending in a ragged band of wind-deformed conifers, bare scree and old snowfield beginning above, a single tall podocarp survivor standing sixty yards above its companions in the open, one branch flagged hard to the east, the tree visibly losing.

Avalanche debris field three seasons old, the snapped trunks of a dozen Araucaria laid parallel downslope, bark bleached silver, the root balls of two still standing upright like walls, young conifer regeneration knee-high in the gap, snow compressing it, the scar flanked by intact dark forest on both sides.

Cloud-layer emergence at dawn, the upper forest rising through a cloud inversion, podocarp crowns breaking the cloud surface across a half-mile ridge, each emergent crown catching first pale sun from above, the cloud below smooth and white as packed snow, no ground visible, only dark crown-tips floating in cold light.

Frost-rimed giant at the forest margin, its needles loaded so heavily in hoarfrost the branch tips curl downward under the weight, each cone along the lower branches encased in clear ice, the whole tree ticking and creaking in the morning cold, a small patch of rust-orange lichen on the trunk base warm against all that white.

Wind-flagged conifer pair on an exposed col, two Araucaria leaning in unison at the same angle, their combined branch mass swept into a single downwind flag forty feet long, snow packed dense on every horizontal surface facing into the wind, the rock around their roots bare and ice-polished, dark and cold.

Krummholz ancient mat on a boulder field, the trees so old and compressed their wood is almost stone, no individual trunk distinguishable in the mass, snow filling the interior channels blue-white, the outer edge of the mat wind-blasted bare on one side, a warm copper smear of dying needles at the very margin.

Mega-conifer snow cathedral at dusk, six podocarps spaced like nave pillars, their boughs meeting overhead and loaded with snow so the interior is a vaulted space of hanging white and deep cobalt shadow, the far end of the row catching last pale light, the near end in darkness already, all of it very cold and very still.

Moss boulder garden in a frozen hollow, seven granite boulders each the size of a small house, mosses on their upper surfaces frozen solid and dark grey-green, lichen in pale gold-ochre crescents along the sun-facing edges, ice glazing the lower halves smooth, the canopy above them open enough for snow to have loaded every flat surface.

The tree-line seen from above, standing on bare rock and looking down at the forest canopy below, the tops of the Araucaria stand packed close and dark, then thinning, then individual crowns spaced apart, then a last few solitary trees, then snowfield, the transition spanning two hundred vertical feet of slope, clean and irreversible.

Avalanche scar in fresh snow, the break happened this season, raw wood showing pale cream at the snap points on thirty trunks, the debris buried but the snapped stumps standing in a line, snow already smoothing the rubble below, two surviving Araucaria at the scar edge standing stripped of half their branches, still upright.

Wind-flagged ridge conifer, a single ancient Araucaria on an exposed spine of rock, its trunk leaning five degrees, its entire crown a one-sided flag of dark blue-green needles streaming east, the west-facing bark silver and bare, snow in a hard curving drift at its base, ochre lichen thick on the rock around its roots.

Frost-rimed forest margin, twenty podocarps along the edge of the tree-line each furred tip to base in hoarfrost, the collective effect a white wall of crystal against the dark interior forest behind, low pale winter sun on the outer faces, every needle tip catching light separately, the shadow within the stand a saturated cobalt.

Cloud-layer forest interior, standing inside a podocarp stand that has entered a cloud, visibility dropping to thirty feet, every trunk dripping with cloud condensation running in black lines down the bark, snow on the boughs absorbing moisture and turning heavy, the tops of the trees invisible above, only trunks descending into white silence.

Wind-flagged Araucaria stand, trunks tilted ten degrees northeast, every branch stripped to leeward and packed with crusted snow on the windward face, dark wet bark near-black against a cobalt shadow canyon, one rust-orange shrub at the base catching the only warmth in a mile of cold blue.

Ancient podocarp cathedral, twelve trunks each eight feet across, boughs carrying three feet of unbroken snow bent to forty-five degrees, blue shadow tunnels between columns of dark bark, pale low-angle sun splitting one lit face from floor to crown, the light surgical and cold.

Krummholz mat of flattened Mesozoic conifers pressed belly-flat across a granite shelf, centuries old and never taller than a man's knee, branches interlocked like a frozen net, snow drifted through every gap in hard blue ridges, the nearest trunk thicker than a thigh and growing sideways.

Tree-line on the north face of a ridge, the forest stopping abruptly halfway up the slope, three solitary podocarps standing thirty feet beyond the last dense stand like sentinels in open snowfield, bare scoured rock above them, the boundary between living and lifeless drawn in one brutal horizontal.

Frost-rimed Araucaria, every needle on every bough furred in two centimeters of hoarfrost crystal, the whole two-hundred-foot tree white and glittering against a deep cobalt sky, breath-fog cold radiating from the canopy, one ochre lichen patch on the upper trunk giving the only warmth in the frame.

Avalanche scar cutting a three-hundred-foot swath through the old-growth conifer stand, snapped trunks silvered and barkless lying in crossed stacks, new seedling conifers eight inches tall pushing up through undisturbed snow between the wreckage, the exposed hillside raw pale rock and ice above the debris field.

Cloud-layer forest with the upper crowns of forty-foot podocarps emerging from a flat white cloud deck, only the top eight feet of each tree visible, dark blue-green needles against blank white ceiling, the forest below dissolved entirely, three crowns catching pale sun from above the cloud while the trunks stand in cold white nothing.

Krummholz field across a boulder-strewn plateau at twelve hundred meters, ancient conifers grown horizontal across the rock surface, each a dense matted carpet no taller than fifty centimeters, the oldest trunks twisted into corkscrew knots of dark wood, a copper-needled dead branch at the center catching the only color for a hundred meters.

Wind-flagged conifer stand on the exposed ridge shoulder, eight trees all swept identically southwest, branches extending six meters downwind and trimmed to bare stubs on the upwind side, snow packed into the armpit of each major branch, cobalt shadow on the ground below running in parallel diagonal lines from every trunk.

Frost-rimed giant podocarp at the edge of a snowfield, every cone on its lower boughs enclosed in clear ice from a freeze-thaw cycle, the cones visible through the glaze like specimens in glass, dark trunk wet from snowmelt at the base, pale sun on the frosted upper canopy reading near-white against slate-blue sky.

Moss and lichen rock garden beneath the old-growth canopy, five house-sized granite boulders furred in frozen dark moss and pale celadon lichen, meltwater ice glazing their south faces in clear sheets, cobalt shadow beneath each boulder deep enough to swallow a vehicle, one smear of rust-orange lichen on the tallest rock's crown.

Tree-line crossing the east slope, dense conifer stand giving way in forty meters to open snowfield and bare talus, the last trees at the boundary stunted to half their inland height, one full-sized Araucaria standing alone two hundred meters above the line in the open snowfield, impossible and enormous, flagged savagely to one side.

Snow-loaded mega-conifer cathedral of Araucaria, the lowest boughs fifteen meters up each carrying a solid mass of snow two meters thick across their full six-meter span, the weight bending them to near-vertical, blue shadow between every trunk, pale cyan light filtering down from the snow-covered canopy like light through ice.

Avalanche runout zone at the forest base, a fan of shattered conifer trunks and compressed snow two meters deep spread across four hundred meters of flat ground, individual trunks stripped of bark and polished smooth by the slide, one living conifer at the fan's edge still standing with its root ball half-exposed, rust-orange heartwood split open.

Frost-rimed understory layer three meters off the ground, smaller conifer saplings ten to twenty feet tall entirely encased in hoarfrost, the crystals on every needle half a centimeter long, the whole layer turned to white lace against near-black wet trunks behind them, breath-fog cold visible as a faint blue haze between the trees.

Krummholz terrace on a wind-scoured ledge, the flattened conifer mat spreading six meters from a cliff face where it is protected just enough to survive, the outermost branches at the exposed edge pruned to bare dead stubs by ice-blasting wind, centuries of growth visible in the layered mat, ochre lichen colonizing the dead wood perimeter.

Wind-flagged stand of six ancient podocarps on a knife-edge ridge, every trunk leaning eight degrees off vertical, branches forming solid pennants pointing south, the ground below packed to blue ice by wind scour, snow built in a hard cornice on the north side of each trunk, the sky behind a saturated deep cobalt with no cloud.

Snow-loaded cathedral of dark-trunked conifers thirty meters across and open in the center like a nave, the boughs from opposing trees meeting overhead under their snow load, blue shadow filling the interior completely, one shaft of pale low-angle sun penetrating a gap and lighting a column of suspended ice crystals from crown to floor.

Moss and lichen boulder cluster, seven boulders each the size of a small house arranged where a glacier dropped them, frozen moss coating every north face in dark blue-green, pale lichen mapping the south faces in silver-celadon, ice glazing the lower halves in a continuous clear sheet cracked in a grid of hexagonal stress fractures.

Cloud-layer forest on the upper approach, the tree-line rising into a stationary cloud bank, individual podocarps becoming silhouettes at fifty meters, dissolving to grey-blue shapes at a hundred, disappearing entirely at one-fifty, the cloud base textured from below by the crowns pressing into it, cold white above and dark trunks below in deep cobalt shadow.

Tree-line on a cirque wall, the forest ending on a curved slope that mirrors the basin's shape, the boundary tracing a clean arc five hundred meters wide, above it nothing but ice-polished rock and permanent snowfield, below it dense dark canopy, one copper-needled dying conifer stranded ten meters above the line in the bare zone.

Frost-rimed Araucaria grove of nine trees at dawn, the hoarfrost at its maximum accumulation, individual crystals on the outermost needles catching the first light at angles that split it into cold blue and pale white, the trees reading as architectural shapes of white against the dark forest interior, each trunk's shadow a hard cobalt line on snow.

Avalanche scar at mid-slope, the scar path sixty meters wide and four hundred meters long, the upper edge a clean break where the snowpack released against a rock band, the lower edge where the slide stopped marked by a wall of compacted debris three meters high, bare rock exposed on the scar floor, silver deadfall trunks in chaos below.

Wind-flagged mega-conifer stand on the exposed plateau, the largest trunk four meters across at the base and flagged so severely the crown extends ten meters downwind and barely one meter upwind, the windward bark sandblasted pale by ice crystals, the lee side dark and wet, a single rust-orange shrub wedged in the root buttresses at ground level.

Moss and lichen colony on a cliff face at the snowline, the vertical rock surface furred from ground to three meters in frozen dark moss, pale lichen spreading in circular colonies from fist-size to two meters across, meltwater seeping through both and freezing in vertical curtains of clear ice over the surface, the cliff face a dark wet mirror below the ice.

Snow-loaded podocarp with a single bough failure, a branch six meters long and a meter in diameter crashed to the snow below under its load, the break a fresh pale wound on the trunk, the fallen bough half-buried already, the remaining upper boughs redistributing their snow load and bending incrementally further as the weight shifts, the trunk unwounded above.

Krummholz peninsula at the tree-line, the flattened conifer mat extending twenty meters out onto open rock from the last upright trees, each plant at the leading edge lower and more compressed than the one behind, the very outermost growth a five-centimeter-high crust of living wood indistinguishable from lichen, snow filling every hollow between the branches.

Cloud-layer forest emerging from below a temperature inversion, the forest canopy below the cloud completely ice-rimed from days of freezing fog, the tops of the tallest trees punching through into clear cold air above, the transition at the cloud surface marked by a sudden change from white ice-covered boughs to dark green ice-free needles above.

Frost-rimed conifer at the boulder field edge, the tree forty meters tall with its upper thirty meters white with hoarfrost and its lowest ten meters bare and dark from the boulder field's thermal mass, the line between frosted and bare running perfectly horizontal around the trunk, one ochre lichen patch below the frost line vivid against dark wet bark.

Wind-flagged stand in a valley notch where prevailing wind funnels through a gap in the ridge, ten trees so severely flagged their crown silhouettes are indistinguishable from each other at distance, forming a single solid form like smoke frozen mid-stream, the snow scoured from the ground beneath them to bare blue ice, cobalt shadow everything.

Avalanche debris field grown over by forty years of recovery, the original snapped trunks now half-decayed and snow-draped, young conifers four to six meters tall growing up through the debris in the gap, the gap still visible from above as a lighter stripe in the dark canopy, copper-needled dead wood emerging from snow where the oldest debris is still exposed.

Moss and lichen rock garden in full frost, the frozen moss on each boulder's north face rigid and dark as cast iron, the lichen on the south faces pale silver-celadon and brittle, meltwater ice columns two centimeters thick connecting boulder edges to the ground below, the whole garden locked and still under a flat pale sky, cobalt shadows pooled at every base.

Tree-line on the windward face of a high ridge, the forest not tapering gradually but cutting off in fewer than twenty meters from full-canopy to bare rock, the last standing trees at the edge each a different degree of distortion and damage, the tallest still thirty meters but stripped to bare branches on its upper half, bare snowfield beginning immediately behind it.

Snow-loaded podocarp cathedral, thirty trunks rising sixty feet before the first branch, each bough bent near-vertical under a meter of snow, shadow between them so deep it reads near-black, pale low-angle sun cutting one bright slot across the white-loaded crowns

Krummholz belt at the snowline, ancient conifers pressed flat across granite slabs by centuries of wind, no trunk taller than a human knee, snow drifted in smooth white pillows through the matted branches, ochre lichen crusting the exposed rock between each sprawling form

Tree-line boundary crossing a north-facing slope, dense conifer forest ending in a clean ragged edge a third of the way up, bare grey rockfield and open snowfield above, three lone survivors standing past the line like sentinels, their flagged crowns the last dark marks before open sky

Frost-rimed mega-conifer, every needle on a two-hundred-foot Araucaria furred white with hoarfrost, each cone glittering under low sun like a lantern, breath-fog cold hanging visible in the blue shadow beneath, the lit face of the crown burning sharp white against a slate-blue ridge behind

Avalanche scar cutting the forest, a hundred-meter-wide corridor of snapped trunks silvered and bare, largest trunks three feet across and splintered mid-height, young conifer seedlings pushing six inches above the snow surface in tight green clusters where the gap opened the canopy

Wind-flagged conifer ridge-line, a dozen ancient trees all leaning east at the same angle as though folded by one enormous hand, snow crusted on the leeside of each trunk, bare rock exposed on windward faces, one rust-orange scrub bush wedged in a crack at the base of the largest tree

Frost-rimed boulder garden, house-sized granite blocks under the outer canopy furred entirely in frozen grey-green moss, meltwater ice glazing their south faces in clear sheets, hoarfrost on every moss-tip catching low sun in cold sparks, deep cobalt shadow pooled under each boulder's overhang

Snow-loaded Araucaria grove, boughs thick as a man's torso bent downward under snow loads until their tips brush the drift below, the weight having shaped each tree into a series of white arches, dark wet trunk centers visible through the frame of each loaded branch

Krummholz island on a granite shelf, a single ancient conifer pressed flat by wind into a circular mat eight meters wide and thirty centimeters tall, snow banked against its upwind edge in a smooth white ramp, the leeward side open to bare rock, every exposed branch polished silver by ice-blast

Tree-line spur, the forest climbing a southwest ridge and dying out abruptly where the rock steepens, the last dozen trees smaller than the ones below them, then a single giant outlier standing alone fifty meters above the line on a ledge, its flagged crown the only dark shape on the white upper slope

Frost-rimed conifer pair, two tall podocarps standing close enough that their furred crowns touch, hoarfrost coating every surface so completely that the trees read as white sculptures against the dark forest behind, a small copper-needled dead branch fallen at their base the only warm note in the scene

Avalanche debris field, snapped trunks piled in a fan at the base of a chute, some trunks six feet in diameter lying parallel, bark stripped silver, root balls torn up and tilted vertical, snow filling every gap between the timber, a streak of rust-orange bark exposed on one freshly broken trunk

Moss-garden under the cathedral canopy, a cluster of ten boulders each the size of a small building, every surface furred in frozen dark green and grey-white moss, meltwater channels frozen into clear ice ribbons down their faces, the air between them cold enough to see breath, blue shadow deep between each mass

Wind-flagged slope forest, forty trees on a windward hillside all carrying their branch mass on the downslope side only, the upslope face of each trunk bare and dark-wet, snow lines defining every horizontal crack in the bark, the collective silhouette of the stand reading as a single swept dark shape

Cloud-layer emergence, a tall Araucaria grove climbing into a low cloud base so that only the top twenty feet of each tree protrude above the flat white deck, the emerging crowns dark against bright overcast, between them wisps of cloud drifting through as the deck breathes slowly upslope

Snow-loaded bough sequence, a single massive podocarp branch forty feet long carrying three distinct snow shelves where the branch forks, each shelf half a meter deep and blue-shadowed on its underside, the branch itself bent to a shallow U under the accumulated weight, creaking in a slow cold wind

Krummholz field across a high col, a continuous carpet of wind-flattened conifers covering fifty meters of exposed saddle, the mats pressing into every hollow in the rock, snow leveling the surface above them into an almost flat white plane, individual trunks only visible where wind has scoured the snow back

Tree-line cliff-face, the forest growing up a talus slope and stopping at a clean horizontal line where the rock face begins, vertical grey stone above streaked with ice seepage frozen white, the uppermost conifers pressed against the rock base as though sheltering, their crowns brushing the cliff foot

Frost-rimed deadfall, a fallen giant four feet across lying half-buried in the snowfield, every inch of exposed bark and every broken branch-stub furred in hoarfrost so thick the surface reads white, the shadow on its underside a deep glacial cyan, a smear of ochre lichen on the exposed root-plate

Avalanche chute with standing ghosts, the scar channel showing three snapped trunks still upright at mid-height, their upper halves gone, the broken tops silver and bare, the channel floor a smooth white ramp of compacted snow between them, new dark-green seedlings clustered around the base of each stump

Cloud-forest understorey, the lower forest submerged in cloud so thick the trunks beyond twenty feet read only as dark vertical smears, the ground visible as a blue-white plane of snow, scattered frost-furred boulders emerging from the white as vague shapes, only the nearest trunks showing their full dark-wet bark

Wind-flagged tree-line survivor, a single enormous Araucaria standing twenty meters past the tree-line, all branch mass swept east into a flat fan half the width of the tree's height, the trunk so leaned that its shadow falls nearly horizontal at midday, cobalt shadow pooling in the drift at its base

Snow-loaded conifer avenue, two rows of tall dark podocarps lining a natural drainage corridor, their loaded boughs arching toward each other overhead to form a broken white tunnel, light filtering through the gaps between snow shelves in cold blue-white shafts, the path below knee-deep in soft drift

Moss and lichen boulder cascade, a slope of boulders each two to four meters across tumbling down into the forest edge, every surface layered in pale grey-green and white lichen, the lichen texture visible as tight rosettes under low-angle light, ice glazing the north faces, the only warm note a rust-orange lichen patch on the largest block

Frost-rimed conifer stand at dawn, four tall trees catching first light across their hoarfrosted east faces, the frost lit white-gold for one minute before the sun angle drops too shallow, blue-shadow still solid on the west side of each trunk, the contrast between the lit and shadowed faces sharp and severe

Krummholz at ice-edge, ancient prostrate conifers growing to the margin of a permanent snowfield and stopping, their outermost branches buried under the snow edge and emerging again downslope as dead silver sticks, the boundary between green living mat and white snow drawn in a ragged irregular line across the rock

Tree-line panorama, the forest visible as a dark mass across an entire valley floor, the tree-line rising to different elevations on each aspect, highest on the south faces and lowest on north, bare pale rock and ice above each dark edge, the whole readable as a single vast pattern of dark and white

Snow-loaded mega-conifer seen from below, standing at the trunk base of a two-hundred-foot Araucaria and looking up, the boughs above diminishing in perspective, each one carrying its snow load, the sky between them a deep cobalt slot, the trunk itself near-black wet bark scaling off in pale plates

Avalanche scar regeneration, the gap cut by an old slide now carrying a dense stand of young conifers two to four meters tall, dark green needles bright against white, their small boughs carrying first-year snow loads, the silvered wreckage of the original stand still visible as stumps and grey logs beneath them

Cloud-layer forest ridge, the forest canopy on a high ridge appearing to float above the cloud deck filling the valley below, the tops of the tallest trees isolated as dark islands in a flat white sea, the ridge itself invisible, only the vertical dark lines of the upper trunks marking where land ends

Wind-flagged forest edge profile, standing at the side of a flagged-conifer stand and reading each tree's swept silhouette against the open snowfield beyond, every crown a horizontal dark brush-stroke pointing the same direction, the snow packed between the trunks glowing pale cyan in the shade, one small copper-leafed shrub at the forest margin the single warm mark in the scene

Wind-flagged Araucaria stand, thirty trunks leaning east like broken masts, every branch swept hard to leeward, snow packed in thick ridges on the sheltered side, needles dark blue-green against a cobalt sky, one dying tree shedding rust-orange bark in strips

Snow-loaded podocarp cathedral, eight trees over two hundred feet tall, boughs bent double under snow loads the weight of stone, dark wet trunks spaced thirty feet apart, deep glacial-blue shadow pooling between them, the silence absolute and pressurised with cold

Krummholz field at fourteen thousand feet, ancient conifers no taller than a man's knee, flattened across exposed granite by four centuries of wind, their trunks corkscrewed and pale as bone, snow drifted through them in smooth sculpted ramps, one seam of ochre lichen splitting the rock beneath

The tree-line crossing a north-facing slope, dense podocarp forest ending in a ragged horizontal line two thirds of the way up, three solitary survivors standing beyond it in open snowfield, their silhouettes black and skeletal against bare white, nothing above them but pale sky and ice

Frost-rimed Araucaria grove, every needle on six giants furred in hoarfrost thick as fur, the ice catching a low-angle sun and firing back cold white light, each cone encased in clear glaze, breath-fog hanging motionless in the air between the trunks, the cold readable in the stillness of it

Avalanche scar cutting through old podocarp forest, a corridor sixty feet wide of snapped trunks silvered and leafless, the break line visible as a clean horizontal wound in the canopy, young conifers eight feet tall pushing up through the snow in the gap, one copper-needled dead tree still standing at the edge

Moss and lichen boulders below the canopy, four house-sized granite blocks furred entirely in frozen moss the colour of deep slate, pale lichen crusting their upper faces in irregular maps, meltwater ice glazing their vertical sides in clear sheets, snow bridging the gaps between them in arching drifts

Cloud-layer forest on the upper ridge, podocarp crowns emerging from a flat sea of cloud at the two-hundred-foot mark, tops visible and sharply lit by low sun against a cobalt sky, everything below the cloud deck dissolved in cold white, the cloud surface smooth as a frozen lake

Wind-flagged conifer wall at the pass, fifty trees standing in a dense line perpendicular to the prevailing west wind, every crown blown flat to the east in identical posture, trunks dark and wet, snow packed in the angle between each trunk and its flagged branches, one exposed root cluster bright with rust-orange moss

Snow-loaded mega-conifer in a bowl below the cirque, a single Araucaria a hundred and ninety feet tall, its lowest boughs nearly touching the snow under their load, the load on each bough measurable in feet not inches, its shadow cast sixty feet long and cobalt-blue across the unbroken drift below

Krummholz at the exposed col, ancient trees pressed flat across pale rock in mats no thicker than a man's thigh, their growth rings countable in the hundreds, snow drifted smooth over them so only their outermost twigs show, the rock between them glazed amber where low sun catches exposed feldspar, everything else ice-white and shadow-blue
